subject: Chemistry
question_text:
The average velocity of gas molecules is 400 m/sec calculate its
r.m.s. velocity at the same temperature
explanation:
$U_{av} = \sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}}$ and
$U_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$
$\therefore\frac{U_{av}}{U_{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}} \times \sqrt{\frac{M}{3RT}} = \sqrt{\frac{8}{3\pi}} = 0.9216$
or $U_{av} = 0.9216 \times U_{rms}$
Given $U_{av} = 400m/s$
$U_{rms} = \frac{400}{0.9216} = 434.02m/s$

oxyacids increases.

question_text:
Calculate the energy required to excite one litre Hydrogen gas
at 1 atm and 298 K to first excited state of atomic hydrogen. The energy
for the dissociation of H-H bond is 436 kJ mol-1.
explanation:
Determination of number of moles of hydrogen gas
$n = \frac{PV}{RT} = \frac{1 \times 1}{0.082 \times 298} = 0.0409$
The concerned reaction is
$H_{2} \longrightarrow 2H;\Delta H = kJ{mol}^{- 1}$
Energy required to bring 0.0409 moles of hydrogen gas to atomic state
$= 436 \times 0.0409 = 17.83kJ$
1 mole of H2 gas has 6.02 × 1023 molecules
0.0409 mole of H2 gas $= \frac{6.02 \times 10^{23}}{1} \times 0.0409$
Since 1 molecule of H2 gas has 2 hydrogen atoms
6.02 × 1023 × 0.0409 molecules of H2 gas
$= 2 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} \times 0.0409\ $
$= 4.92 \times 10^{22}\ atoms$
Energy required to excite an electron from the ground state to the next
excited state
$= 13.6\left( \frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}} \right)eV = 13.6 \times \left( \frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{4} \right) = 13.6 \times \frac{3}{4} = 10.2eV = 1.632 \times 10^{- 21}kJ$
Therefore energy required to excite 4.92 × 1022 electrons
$= 1.632 \times 10^{- 21} \times 4.92 \times 10^{22}kJ$
$= 8.03 \times 10 = 80.3kJ$
Therefore total energy required $= 17.83 + 80.3 = 98.17kJ$

question_text:
Metallic magnesium has a hexagonal close-packed structure and a
density of 1.74 g/cm3. Assume magnesium atoms to be spheres of radius r.
74.1 of the space are occupied by atoms. Calculate the volume of each
atom and the atomic radius r. (Mg = 24.31)
explanation:
Packing efficiency of hcp
$= \frac{6\ \times \ vol.\ \ of\ 1\ atom}{Vol.\ \ of\ unit\ cell}$
Volume of unit cell $= \frac{Z \times M}{N_{A} \times d}$
$= \frac{6 \times 24.31}{6.023 \times 10^{23} \times 1.74}$
$= 13.9179 \times 10^{- 23}{cm}^{3}$
So, volume of 1 atom
$= \frac{Packing\ fraction \times Vol.\ of\ unit\ cell}{6}$
$= \frac{0.741 \times 13.9179 \times 10^{- 23}}{6}$
$= 1.718 \times 10^{- 22}{cm}^{3}$
Volume of 1 atom $= \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$
Radius of 1 atom
$= (r) = {(\frac{Volume\ \ of\ 1\ atom \times 3}{4\pi})}^{1/3}$
$= {(0.41055 \times 10^{- 23})}^{1/3} = 1.60Å.$

subject: Chemistry
question_text:
Which one of the following is least reactive in a nucleophilic
substitution reaction?
explanation:
The non reactivity of the chlorine atom in vinyl chloride may
be explained from the molecular orbital point of view as follows. If the
chlorine atom has sp^2 hybridization the C -Cl bond will be a σ bond
and the two lone pairs of electron would occupy the other two
[IMAGE] orbitals. This would leave a p -orbital
containing a lone pair and this orbital could not conjugate with the π
bond of the ethylenic link. Thus two M.O.S. will be required to
accommodate these four π electrons. Furthermore since chlorine is more
electronegative than carbon, the electron will tend to be found in the
chlorine atom has now lost full control of the one pair and so, is less
negative than it would have been had there been no conjugation. Since
two carbon atoms have acquired a share in the lone pair, each atom
acquires a small negative charge. Hence, owing to delocalization of
bonds (through conjugation), the vinyl chloride molecule has an
increased stability. Before the chlorine atom can be displaced by some
other group the lone pair must be localized again on the chlorine atom.
This requires energy and so the chlorine is more firmly bound than has
no conjugation occurred.

question_text:
A gaseous mixture of three gases A, B and C has a pressure of 10
atm. The total number of moles of all the gases is 10. If the partial
pressure of A and B are 3.0 and 1.0 atm respectively and if C has mol.
wt. of 2.0, what is the weight of C in g present in the mixture ?
explanation:
Pressure of Total mixture = 10 atm
$P_{A} + P_{B} + P_{c} = 10$
$3 + 1 + P_{c} = 10 \Rightarrow P_{c} = 6\ atm\ $
Total moles of mixture = 10
$N_{A} + n_{B} + n_{C} = 10$
$\frac{P_{A}}{P_{B}} = \frac{n_{A}}{n_{B}} = \frac{3}{1} \Rightarrow \frac{P_{B}}{P_{C}} = \frac{n_{B}}{n_{C}} = \frac{1}{6}$
Let
$n_{A} = K \Rightarrow n_{B} = \frac{K}{3}n_{c} = \frac{1}{6}n_{B} = 2K$
$\Rightarrow K + \frac{K}{3} + 2K = 10 \Rightarrow \frac{K}{3} = \frac{n_{C}}{6} \Rightarrow n_{c} = 2K$
$\Rightarrow K\left( \frac{10}{3} \right) = 10K = 3, \Rightarrow n_{A} = 3$
$n_{B} = 1$
$n_{c} = 6$
weight of in mixture =.$\ = 2 \times 6 = 12$

question_text:
What volume of 98 sulphuric acid (in ml) should be mixed with
water to obtain 200 mL of 15 solution of sulphuric acid by weight ?
Given density of H2O = 1.00 g cm^-3, sulphuric acid (98 ) = 1.88 g
cm-3 and sulphuric acid (15 ) = 1.12 g cm-3.
explanation:
It is a case of dilution, simplest way is to determine
normality of the 98 and 15 H2SO4.
(i) For 98 H2SO4: 100 g H2SO4 solution $= \frac{100}{1.88}{cm}^{3}$
solution has H2SO4 = 98 g
$N_{1}(98\%) = \frac{1000w_{1}}{E_{1}V} = \frac{1000 \times 98}{49 \times \frac{100}{1.88}} = 37.6N$
where w1 is the weight of solute of equivalent weight E1 in V mL
solution
(ii) For 15 H2SO4: 100 g H2SO4 solution $= \frac{100}{1.12}{cm}^{3}$
has H2SO4 = 15 g
$N_{2}(15\%) = \frac{1000w_{1}}{E_{1}V} = \frac{1000 \times 15}{49 \times \frac{100}{1.12}} = 3.43$
Using $N_{1}V_{1} = N_{2}V_{2}$
$37.6 \times V_{1} = 3.43 \times 200$
$V_{1} = 18.2mL$

explanation:

But for y=1, x=2
$2x^{2} - 3xy + y^{2} = 2x(2)^{2} - 3 \times 1 \times 2 + (1)^{2} = 8 - 6 + 1 = 3 \neq 0$
So 1 R 2 but 2 not R 1
So R is not symmetric.

question_text:
A spherical balloon is filled with $4500_{\pi}$ cubic meters of
helium gas. If a leak in the balloon causes the gas to escape at the
rate of $72_{\pi}$ cubic meters per minute then the rate (in meters per
minute) at which the radius of the balloon decreases 49 minutes after
the leakage began is
explanation:
Let r be the radius of the balloon and V be its volume. It is
given that
$\frac{dV}{dt} = - 72\pi$
$\frac{d}{dt}\left( \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} \right) = - 72\pi \Rightarrow \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = - 72\pi t + C$
When $t = 0,\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = C = 4500\pi$
$\therefore\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = 4500\pi - 72\pi t$
When $t = 49,\frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = 4500\pi - (72\pi)(49) = 972\pi$
$\Rightarrow$ r^3 = 729  so  r = 9
Also $\frac{d}{dt}\left( \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} \right) = - 72\pi$
$\Rightarrow 4\pi r^{2}\frac{dr}{dt} = - 72\pi$
$\Rightarrow \frac{dr}{dt} = - \frac{72\pi}{4\pi r^{2}} = - \frac{18}{r^{2}}$.
 So ${\frac{dr}{dt}|}_{r = 9} = - \frac{2}{9}$.

question_text:
In $\Delta$ABC internal angle bisectors AI, BI and CI are
produced to meet opposite sides in C', respectively.
Find the maximum value of
$\frac{27(AI \times BI \times CI)}{{AA}^{'} \times {BB}^{'} \times {CC}^{'}}$
explanation:
Since angle bisector divides opposite sides in ratio of sides
containing the angle, hence
${BA}^{'} = \frac{ac}{b + c},{CA}^{'} = \frac{ab}{b + c}$
now BI is also an angle bisector of $\angle$B for triangle ABA'.
$\therefore\frac{AI}{A^{'}I} = \frac{b + c}{a} \Rightarrow \frac{AI}{{AA}^{'}} = \frac{b + c}{a + b + c}$
Similarly,
$\frac{BI}{{BB}^{'}} = \frac{a + c}{a + b + c}$ and
$\frac{CI}{{CC}^{'}} = \frac{a + b}{a + b + c}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{AI \times BI \times CI}{AA^{'} \times BB^{'} \times CC^{'}} = \frac{(a + b)(b + c)(c + a)}{(a + b + c)^{3}}$
Using A.M. $\geq$ G.M. we get
$\frac{2(a + b + c)}{3(a + b + c)} \geq \left\lbrack \frac{(a + b)(b + c)(c + a)}{(a + b + c)^{3}} \right\rbrack^{\frac{1}{3}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{(a + b)(b + c)(c + a)}{(a + b + c)^{3}} \leq \frac{8}{27}$
$\therefore$ maximum value
$\frac{27(AI \times BI \times CI)}{{AA}^{'} \times {BB}^{'} \times {CC}^{'}} = 8$

$\Delta U = \frac{nf}{2}R\Delta T = \frac{f}{2}P\Delta V = \frac{3}{2}P_{0}\left( 2V_{0} \right) = 3P_{0}V_{0}$
$\therefore\Delta Q = 7P_{0}V_{0}$

question_text:
Two identical wires A and B, each of length $\mathcal{l}$, carry
the same current I. Wire A is bent into acircle of radius R and wire B
is bent form a squareof side a. If B_Aand B_B are the values of
magnetic field at the centres of the circle and square respectively,
then the ratio B_A/ B_B is$\pi^{2}:n\sqrt{2}.\ $What is the value of
n.
explanation:
B at centre of a circle $= \frac{\mu_{0}I}{2R}$
B at centre of a
square $= 4 \times \frac{\mu I}{4\pi \cdot \frac{\mathcal{l}}{2}}\left( sin45^{\circ} + sin45^{\circ} \right)$
$= 4\sqrt{2}\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi\mathcal{l}}$
 Now, $R = \frac{L}{2\pi}\ $and $\mathcal{l =}\frac{L}{4}(\ as\ L = 2\pi R = 4\mathcal{l)}$
 Where, L= length of wire 
$\therefore{\ \ \ B}_{A} = \frac{\mu_{0}L}{2 \cdot \frac{L}{2\pi}} = \frac{\pi\mu_{0}I}{L} = \pi\left( \frac{\mu_{0}I}{L} \right)$
$B_{B} = 4\sqrt{2}\frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi\left( \frac{L}{4} \right)} = \frac{8\sqrt{2}\mu_{0}I}{\pi L} = \frac{8\sqrt{2}}{\pi}\left( \frac{\mu_{0}I}{L} \right)$
$\therefore{\ \ \ \ B}_{A}:B_{B} = \pi^{2}:8\sqrt{2}$

Water flows in a horizontal tube (see figure). The pressure of
water changes by 700 Nm-2 between A and B where the area of cross
section are [IMAGE] and [IMAGE], respectively. Find the rate of flow of water
through the tube. (density of water [IMAGE] )

using equation of continuity
$40V_{A} = 20V_{B}$
$\Rightarrow 2V_{A} = V_{B}$
Using Bernoulli's equation
$P_{A} + \frac{1}{2}\rho V_{A}^{2} = P_{B} + \frac{1}{2}\rho V_{B}^{2}$
$\Rightarrow P_{A} - P_{B} = \frac{1}{2}\rho\left( V_{B}^{2} - V_{A}^{2} \right)$
$\Rightarrow \Delta P = \frac{1}{2}1000\left( V_{B}^{2} - \frac{V_{B}^{2}}{4} \right)$
$\Rightarrow \Delta P = 500 \times \frac{3V_{B}^{2}}{4}$
$\Rightarrow V_{B} = \sqrt{\frac{(\Delta P) \times 4}{1500}} = \sqrt{\frac{(700) \times 4}{1500}m/s}$
Volume flow rate $= 20 \times 100 \times V_{B} = 2732{cm}^{3}/s$

question_text:
A thin walled hollow cylinder is closed from both the ends. The
mass of the curved part is m and the mass of each circular part is also
m. The radius of the cylinder is R and its length is 2R. What will be
the moment of inertia of this hollow cylinder about the axis,
perpendicular to its length and passing through its centre of mass?
explanation:
First find I of the hollow tube
$I_{1} = \int\frac{{dmR}^{2}}{2} + \int_{x = - \frac{\mathcal{l}}{2}}^{x = + \frac{\mathcal{l}}{2}}{(\frac{m}{\mathcal{l}}dx)}x^{2}$
$I_{1} = \frac{{mR}^{2}}{2} + \frac{m^{\mathcal{l}^{2}}}{12}$ where
$\mathcal{l} = 2R$
So $I_{1} = \frac{5}{6}{mR}^{2}$
Now moment of inertias of each circular plate about that axis.
$I = \frac{mR^{2}}{4} + mR^{2} = \frac{5}{4}mR^{2}$
$I_{total} = \frac{5}{6}{mR}^{2} + 2 \times \left( \frac{5}{4}{mR}^{2} \right)$
$I_{total} = \frac{10}{3}{mR}^{2}$

A system undergoes three quasi-static processes sequentially as
indicated in the given figure. $1 \rightarrow 2$is an isobaric process,
$2 \rightarrow 3$ is a polytrophic process with

constant.
$P_{2} = P_{1} = 4 \times 10^{5}Nm^{- 2},P_{3} = 1 \times 10^{5}Nm^{- 2}$and$\ V_{1} = 1m^{3}$.

energy is $\Delta U$ and the work done is $\Delta W$. for polytropic
process $PV^{\gamma} =$ constant.
(Take $\mathcal{l}$n2 = 0.693). Then
explanation:
For the process $3 \rightarrow 1$
$P_{1}V_{1} = P_{3}V_{3} \Rightarrow V_{3} = \frac{P_{1}V_{1}}{P_{3}} = \frac{4 \times 10^{5} \times 1}{1 \times 10^{5}} = 4m^{3}$
For the process $2 \rightarrow 3$
$P_{2}V_{2}^{\gamma} = P_{3}V_{3}^{\gamma} \Rightarrow V_{2} = \left( \frac{P_{3}}{P_{2}} \right)^{\frac{1}{\gamma}}V_{3} = 4\left( \frac{1}{4} \right)^{\frac{3}{4}} = 4^{\frac{1}{4}} = \sqrt{2}m^{3}$
For the process $1 \rightarrow 2$
$W_{12} = P_{1}\left( V_{2} - V_{1} \right) = \left( \sqrt{2} - 1 \right)4 \times 10^{5}J$
For the process $2 \rightarrow 3$
$W_{23} = \frac{\left( P_{2}V_{2} - P_{3}V_{3} \right)}{(\gamma - 1)} = 12(\sqrt{2} - 1) \times 10^{5}J$
For the process $3 \rightarrow 1$,
$w_{31} = - P_{1}V_{1}ln\frac{V_{3}}{V_{1}} - 4 \times 10^{5} \times 1 \times ln(4)$
For cyclic process, $\Delta\ U = 0$
$\therefore\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W = \Delta W = 4 \times 10^{5}(\sqrt{2} - 1)$
$1 \rightarrow 2 \rightarrow 3 \rightarrow 1$
$\Delta Q = + 12 \times 10^{5}(\sqrt{2} - 1) - 4 \times 10^{5} \times 2 \times 0.693$
$= 1.08 \times 10^{5}J$

question_text:
A solid sphere of mass m and radius r is gently placed on a
conveyer belt moving with constant velocityV. If the coefficient of
friction between the belt and sphere is$\frac{2}{7}$, the distance
travelled by the centre of the sphere before it starts pure rolling is.
explanation:
Initial situation w.r.t. the conveyer belt:
$\mu mgR = \frac{2}{5}{mR}^{2} \cdot \alpha$ $\Rightarrow$
$\alpha = \frac{5}{7} \cdot \frac{g}{R}$
At pure rolling:
$v^{'} = v - (\mu g)t$and $\omega^{'} = 0 + \left( \frac{5}{7} \cdot \frac{g}{R} \right)t$
(Since at pure rolling)
$\Rightarrow$ $v - \mu gt = \frac{5}{7} \cdot g \cdot t$
$\Rightarrow$ $t = \frac{v}{g}\left( \because\mu = \frac{2}{7} \right)$
For centre of the sphere:$S = v\left( \frac{v}{g} \right) - \frac{1}{2} \cdot \left( \frac{2}{7} \cdot g \right)\left( \frac{v^{2}}{g^{2}} \right)$
$S = \frac{v^{2}}{g} - \frac{v^{2}}{7g}$ (w.r.t. belt)

$\Rightarrow 30 + 9n = 28 + 10n$
$\Rightarrow n = 2$

question_text:
A container of fixed volume has a mixture of one mole of hydrogen
and one mole of helium in equilibrium at temperature T. Assuming the
gases are ideal, the correct statement(s) is (are)

options.text: The average energy per mole of the gas mixture is 2RT.

The ratio of speed of sound in the gas mixture to that in helium
gas is $\sqrt{6/5}$

The ratio of the rms speed of helium atoms to that of hydrogen
molecules is $1/\sqrt{2}$

explanation:
$\ $For hydrogen,$\ n_{1} = 1,C_{v,} = \frac{5}{2}R$
 For mixture of gases,
$C_{v} = \frac{n_{1}C_{V,} + n_{2}C_{V_{2}}}{n_{1} + n_{2}}$
$= \frac{1 \times \frac{5}{2}R + 1 \times \frac{3}{2}R}{1 + 1} = 2R$
$C_{P} = C_{v} + R = 3R,\gamma_{mix} = \frac{C_{P}}{C_{v}} = \frac{3}{2}$
Also, $\gamma_{mx} = 1 + \frac{2}{f} \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2} = 1 + \frac{2}{f}\therefore f = 4$
$\therefore$ Average energy per mole $= \frac{1}{2}fRT = 2RT$
$M_{\max} = \frac{n_{1}M_{1} + n_{2}M_{2}}{n_{1} + n_{2}} = \frac{1 \times 2 + 1 \times 4}{1 + 1} = 3gm{ol}^{- 1}$
 Speed of sound in a gas, $v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma RT}{M}}$
For a given value of T,v$\propto \sqrt{\frac{\gamma}{M}}$
 Rms speed of a gas molecule at temperature T is given by 
$T,v \propto \sqrt{\frac{\gamma}{M}}$
 For a given value of T,$\ v_{rms} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$
$\frac{\left( v_{rms\ } \right)He}{\left( v_{rms\ } \right)H_{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{M_{H_{2}}}{M_{He}}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{4}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
 So, options (a), (b) and (c) are correct

question_text:
A solid cylinder and a solid sphere, both having the same mass
and radius, are released from an inclined plane having angle of
inclination $\theta$ one by one. They roll on the incline without
slipping. The statement that holds good in this motion is

options.text: the force of friction that acts on the two is the same

the force of friction is greater in case of a sphere than for a
cylinder.

the force of friction is greater in case of cylinder than for
sphere.

the force of friction will depend on the nature of the surface
of the body that is moving and that of the inclined surface, and is
independent of the shape and size of the moving body.

explanation:
Equation of motion
$mg\ sin\theta - f = ma$....(i)
$fR = I\alpha = I\frac{a}{R}$
$\Rightarrow f = I\frac{a}{R^{2}}$....(ii)
from (i) and (ii)
$mgsin\theta - f = m.\frac{fR^{2}}{I}$
$mgsin\theta = f(1 + m.\frac{R^{2}}{I}$)
$f = \frac{mgsin\theta}{1 + \frac{mR^{2}}{I}}$
Moment of inertia of solid cylinder is greater, so friction force f will
be greater.
